_meta.description: Government scheme eligibility rules for check_govt_schemes (src/tools.py). Each scheme has one or more eligibility paths; a path is a list of rules that must all pass. Rule strength 'hard' is a fact the user states (unknown -> check); 'proxy' is a signal that cannot be confirmed from a chat profile (e.g. SECC listing), so passing it yields 'check', never 'eligible'. Every rule cites its source.

rule_types.income_pct_fpl_between: min_pct <= household income / FPL(household_size) x 100 <= max_pct, using fpl_year
rule_types.monthly_income_at_most: annual_income / 12 <= max (proxy for a per-earner ceiling)
rule_types.state_not_in: US state is not in values (unknown state -> check)
rule_types.flag_not_true: profile flag is not true (unknown -> check)

_meta.caution: Scheme rules change. The tool reports the rule and source so the user can confirm on the official portal.

2026.source: HHS/ASPE 2026 Poverty Guidelines, 48 contiguous states and DC (in effect 13 Jan 2026)

2025.source: HHS/ASPE 2025 Poverty Guidelines (used for 2026 Marketplace premium tax credits: 400% x 15,650 = $62,600 for one person)

schemes.name: Medicare
schemes.benefit: Hospital (Part A) and medical (Part B) cover; drug cover via Part D
schemes.how_to_apply: Social Security / Medicare.gov; enrolment window around the 65th birthday

rules.source: Medicare.gov: people 65 or older are eligible

paths.label: Under 65 with a qualifying disability (SSDI 24 months, ESRD, ALS)

rules.source: Medicare.gov: some people under 65 qualify through disability

schemes.name: Medicaid (ACA adult expansion)
schemes.benefit: Comprehensive cover with little or no premium

paths.label: Adult under 65, income up to 138% FPL, in an expansion state

rules.source: ACA Medicaid expansion covers non-elderly adults
ACA expansion threshold: 133% FPL plus a 5% income disregard = 138% FPL
KFF, Status of State Action on the Medicaid Expansion Decision (as of October 2026): 41 adopted incl. DC, 10 not adopted

notes: In the 10 non-expansion states most childless adults under 100% FPL get neither Medicaid nor Marketplace subsidies (the 'coverage gap'). Children may still qualify for Medicaid/CHIP at higher incomes.

schemes.name: ACA Marketplace premium tax credit
schemes.benefit: Tax credit that caps the benchmark silver premium at a share of income
schemes.how_to_apply: HealthCare.gov or the state marketplace during open enrolment

paths.label: Income 100-400% FPL, no Medicare/Medicaid, no affordable employer plan

rules.source: KFF (19 May 2026): enhanced tax credits expired after 2025, so eligibility returned to 100-400% FPL ($62,600 for one person in 2026)
People eligible for Medicare cannot get Marketplace tax credits
An offer of affordable employer coverage (employee self-only share <= 9.96% of income in 2026, IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-25) removes eligibility

schemes.name: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY
schemes.benefit: Rs 5 lakh hospital cover per family per year at empanelled hospitals; cashless
schemes.how_to_apply: Check eligibility at beneficiary.nha.gov.in (Aadhaar / ration card) or an Ayushman Mitra at an empanelled hospital

paths.label: Senior citizen 70+ (Ayushman Vay Vandana), any income

rules.source: Cabinet decision, 11 Sep 2024: all senior citizens aged 70 and above eligible irrespective of income; Rs 5 lakh per year (separate top-up if the family is already covered)

paths.label: Household listed under SECC 2011 deprivation / occupational criteria (or a state-expanded list)

rules.source: PM-JAY eligibility follows SECC 2011 deprivation (rural) and occupational (urban) criteria, e.g. landless manual casual labour, street vendors, domestic workers
SECC automatic exclusion: a household member earning more than Rs 10,000 a month (secondary sources; per-member vs household wording differs)

notes: Many states run their own schemes merged with PM-JAY with wider income limits; the portal check is final.

schemes.name: PMJJBY (Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana)
schemes.benefit: Rs 2 lakh life cover, death from any cause; premium Rs 436 a year auto-debited
schemes.how_to_apply: Through your bank or post office savings account (enrol/renew by 31 May each year)

paths.label: Age 18-50 with a savings bank or post office account

rules.source: PIB, PMJJBY 10 years (8 May 2025): ages 18-50 to enrol, cover continues to 55; Rs 2 lakh for Rs 436 a year
PIB (8 May 2025): requires a savings account; premium auto-debited

schemes.name: PMSBY (Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana)
schemes.benefit: Rs 2 lakh for accidental death or total disability, Rs 1 lakh for partial disability; premium Rs 20 a year
schemes.how_to_apply: Through your bank or post office savings account

paths.label: Age 18-70 with a savings bank account

rules.source: Department of Financial Services monthly summary (May 2022): PMSBY premium revised from Rs 12 to Rs 20 w.e.f. 1 Jun 2022; age 18-70 per scheme rules
Scheme requires an Aadhaar-linked savings account

schemes.name: Social Health Authority (SHA) - SHIF, Primary Health Care Fund, ECCIF
schemes.benefit: Primary care free at public facilities; hospital, chronic and emergency cover via SHIF
schemes.how_to_apply: Register at sha.go.ke, *147# or a Huduma centre; informal earners are means-tested

rules.source: Social Health Insurance Act 2023 (No. 16 of 2023): registration is mandatory for every resident

contribution_source.source: Social Health Insurance Regulations 2024: 2.75% of gross household income, minimum KES 300 a month; unsalaried members pay on means-tested income (confirmed via 2026 guides; ira/sha pages block download)

notes: Government pays for households assessed as indigent.
Informal-sector contributions were annual lump sums; the government later allowed pro-rata/monthly payment (Nation, 2025).
